A bank of blue borage grows right up around the hive stands, its nodding star-shaped flowers almost touching the painted timber entrances.
Slate-purple phacelia covers the slope behind the hives in a dense, humming carpet, every flower head curled tight at its tip.
White clover threads through the rough grass between the hive stands, its round pale heads level with the bottom boards.
A lavender row gone deep violet runs in a straight line along the hive front, the woody stems pressed close to the painted sides.
Heather turns the low hill behind the apiary a full, flat purple, spilling right down to the fence post nearest the hives.
Sunflowers lean their heavy brown-centred yellow heads over the fence beside the hives, the tallest one almost brushing the nearest roof.
An old lime tree stands directly over the hives in small green-cream flower, its whole canopy thick and fragrant with blossom.
Crimson field beans grow in a tall, dense block just beyond the hive row, their red-and-black flowers vivid against the green stems.
Apple blossom in white and shell pink arches over two hive roofs from a low spreading tree, petals settling on the flat lids.
A rosemary hedge in pale powdery blue runs along the windward side of the apiary, clipped low enough to see the hive fronts above it.
A strip of oilseed in flat chrome yellow runs away beyond the hedge, bright enough to throw colour back onto the nearest hive side.
Bramble flower in white and the faintest blush sprawls over the drystone wall directly behind the hives, the canes arching loose and unpruned.
A cutting bed of orange calendula and pink cosmos fills the space between the shed and the nearest hive, the colours stacked in loose drifts.
Blue echium spires stand tall at the end of the hive row, their dense flower columns rising well above the rooftops.
A hawthorn hedge in dense, cream-white blossom wraps two sides of the apiary, the flowers packed so tight the stems disappear beneath them.
Buckwheat in pinkish white fills a strip immediately beyond the fence, its flat-headed clusters held on reddish stems at hive-roof height.
A yellow mustard strip runs parallel to the hive row with barely a path between them, the flat acid-yellow flowers at landing-board level.
Scarlet poppies push through a cereal edge at the far corner of the fence, their tissue petals open wide around a black centre.
Teasel and knapweed gone mauve stand in a rough clump at the apiary corner, their spiky heads above the fence line and nodding slightly.
A willow leans over the hive nearest the stream, its branches heavy with soft yellow-green catkins pressed close to the timber roof.
A drift of yellow-and-brown sunflower heads left standing fills the bed behind the hives, the dried petals still bright against the seed-heavy centres.
Ivy in lime-green flower covers the old stone wall at the hive backs, the flat-topped clusters crowding every surface of the mortar.
A sweet chestnut stands at the field edge and drops its cream tassels onto the hive roofs, the long fluffy strands piling up on the flat lids.
A bed of purple alliums gone to globe-shaped seed-heads crowds the path beside the hives, the spheres held high on bare straight stalks.
A wildflower strip in mixed yellow, white and cornflower blue runs along the fence inside the apiary, every square centimetre of soil taken.
